thread:
maya: Hey team — I'm starting a small refresh of the GreetKit bootstrap tutorial. goal: simplify onboarding for new devs by switching examples to the SDK's 'client.signingKey' flow and adding a single-file docker-compose first-deploy. opening a draft PR shortly. any volunteers for a quick snippet sanity check?

jonah: +1, I can scan the auth snippet tonight. which SDK version are we pinning to?

maya: planning to target sdk@1.10.0 (it adds the ephemeral token helper). I'll update the package.json example.

liz: heads up — link-checker found a dead link in the current doc: the old env var reference page. docs-bot also posted a report earlier.

docs-bot: automated-check: broken-link detected => https://old.docs.redwood.inference/auth/env-vars (404) (reported by link-checker v2)

paul: For the docker-compose example, can we keep it minimal? I suggest a single service running the sample app + a commented env example rather than a full postgres section. Less to maintain.

sam: Agree on minimal compose. Also: on mac M1 the default image requires arm64 tagging — include a note or recommend using node:18-bullseye-slim.

maya: Good catches. I'll: 1) replace old link, 2) update SDK snippet to 1.10.0, 3) add a tiny docker-compose snippet and the mac note, 4) include a short CI test (node 18 & 20). Planning to include a small code snippet for the new signingKey flow.

jonah: Can you paste the signing snippet you plan to use? I can validate the auth headers match the runtime.

maya: Sure — draft here:

```bash
# set env var locally
export RW_API_KEY=sk.test_XXXXX

# minimal Node example using new helper
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
const token = await client.auth.getEphemeralToken({ ttl: 300 });
// then use token for short-lived requests from the client app
```

liz: tiny nit: use `getEphemeralToken({ ttlSeconds: 300 })` to match param name in SDK. also add a note about refreshing the token before reuse.

maya: updated in my head, will reflect in PR.

paul: For the docker-compose snippet, propose:

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  greetkit:
    image: node:18-bullseye-slim
    working_dir: /app
    volumes:
      - ./:/app
    command: sh -c "npm install && npm run start"
    environment:
      - RW_API_KEY=${RW_API_KEY}
```

sam: include a short troubleshooting step: "If you see ECONNREFUSED when calling the API, check that RW_API_KEY is exported and not wrapped in quotes in the .env file"

maya: adding that. also thinking about adding a short migration note: "If you previously used static keys in examples, switch to ephemeral tokens or the server-side signing helper to avoid leaking secrets in client code."

jonah: Quick regression to watch: examples that used `client.generate()` without specifying model now default to 'gtr-mini-v1' in new runtime — add an explicit model selection in the snippet to avoid surprises.

maya: Good call. I'll set model: 'rw/gtr-mini-v1' in examples.

liz: If you want, I can do a pass on copy + links after you open the PR. I have ~30 mins tomorrow morning.

maya: That would be awesome. I'll tag you in the PR description and add a short checklist of things changed.

docs-bot: reminder-scheduled: please run `make docs-linkcheck` before merging (CI job: docs/link-check)

paul: One more suggestion — add a quick visual callout in the tutorial about "Production keys vs ephemeral tokens" with a tiny table (server: long-lived, client: ephemeral).

maya: Will include that table. planning to open PR #5467 (draft) in ~30m with the core changes. If anyone wants to pick up specific checks: liz -> copy/links, jonah -> auth header sanity, sam -> mac image/node notes, paul -> compose minimal example.

jonah: I'll review auth tonight. :eyes:

liz: I'll queue a review slot for 9:30am PT. :+1:

sam: I'll test the compose snippet on M1 later and post results.

maya: Thanks all — will post the draft PR link here when ready. :shipit:
